title.narrative: Skills for Employment Investment Program - Tranche 1

description.narrative: The investment program will support the Government of Bangladesh's reforms in skills development, anchored in the National Skills Development Policy (NSDP), 2011. It will support large-scale private sector involvement and public-private partnership, which is critical to meet existing and future labor market needs and to reduce the skills gap. This in turn is crucial for Bangladesh to move away from the 'low-skill, low-wage equilibriumm' to a 'higher skill, higher wage virtuous cycle' to become a middle income country. The program will help the government to scale-up skilling of new entrants and up-skilling of existing workers to contribute to higher growth of priority sectors. The program will strengthen skills development in Bangladesh and support transition to a sector-wide approach (SWAp) by establishing a unified funding system and enhancing overall coordination of the currently fragmented system.

Progress Toward Outcome: As of 30 June 2021, a total of 279,748 trainees (28.76% or 80,463 females) were enrolled under Tranche 1. Of the enrolled, 267,040 trainees (29.3% or 78,249 females) were certified.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Feb 2023: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/42466/42466-015-apfs-en_3.pdf
Some results are in the Social Monitoring Reports | Jan 2022: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/42466/42466-015-smr-en_7.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: 40,000 trainees (53% or 21,213 females) received special stipend under Tranche 1. 100% target of stipend distribution has been achieved.
As of 30 June 2021, a total of 279,748 trainees were enrolled under Tranche 1. Out of these enrollments, 267,040 trainees (29.3% or 78,249 females) were certified.
As of 30 June 2021, total of 238,558 new entrants were enrolled under Tranche 1. 226, 486 of the new entrants were certified. Out of them, 154,435 have been placed in jobs (68.18% of the certified and 64.80% of the net enrolled). Female job placement against female certification is 73.68%
As of 30 June 2021, total enrollment for up-skilling was 41,190, certification was 40,553 and job placement 36,993. 91.22% of the certified up-skilled workers are still employed which is 89.82% of the net enrolled. Net enrollment was 41,182.
RPL Program has been dropped due to overlapping efforts with the World Bank program.
87 competency standards (CSs) have been developed. Out of this, 50 CSs have been developed by British Council, 35 by the Fast Track Consultants and the rest 02 have been developed by the Industry Associations which have been subsequently validated by SEIP. 47 CSs have so far been approved by BTEB and 12 by NSDA. All CSs are now used for SEIP training.
60 competency-based learning materials (CBLMs) developed. Out of this, 18 developed by British Council has developed 18, 1 by Fast Track Consultant, and 41 by industry associations. The CBLMs are now being used for imparting training
87 assessment tools developed. Out of this,50 developed by British Council, and remaining by the Fast Track Consultant. All assessment tools are being used
2,826 trainers (18.4% or 520 females)
150 (13 females) principals and TVET managers from public and private training providers completed management and refreshers' training from Infrastructure Investment Facilitation Company (IIFC)
205 assessors (6.3% or 13 females) have been trained
Two ISCs- Construction ISC and Light Engineering ISC have been operationalized in 2017 and have been implementing the targeted activities set for them.
National Skills Development Authority (NSDA) established in October 2018. Staff recruitment for NSDA hasn't started yet although Finance Division has cleared the Organogram. It has a budget line to receive regular fiscal allocation from the government similar to other government organizations. The NSDA rules have already been approved by the Cabinet and posted on the website. Fund Utilization Rules of NHRDF, approved by the Cabinet on 4 November 2019, will be implemented by NSDA. NSDA is now almost fully operational.
NHRDF was officially established on 16 May 2017. Under an MoU between NHRDF and SEIP on 07 May 2018, SEIP provided 3-year support (till December 2020) to fully operationalize NHRDF. The Organogram and Recruitment Rules were finalized at a meeting held on 02 January 2020 with Finance Secretary in the Chair. Recruitment is expected to start from January 2021.
Market responsive skills training program is being conducted by 116 public training institutes.
45 Job placement officers have been deployed for providing job placement support to the SEIP graduates.
Unified MTBF for skills development may be considered in the future by NSDA. This is beyond the scope of SEIP.
SDCMU became operational in December 2014.
SWAp is actually not within the scope of SEIP as it involves multiple ministries and divisions. NSDA can consider taking necessary steps to develop SWAp roadmap and framework in the future. It will certainly need government's approval as it involves multiple stakeholders.
TMS has been established and operationalized in 2015. Special Stipend Module, Mobile App for Attendance, Dash Board for TMS showing enrollment, certification, and job placement data have been incorporated. Monitoring Module is under development and will be completed by December 2020.
Final report for the tracer study submitted in April 2019. The tracer study also includes employer's satisfaction survey. First round of skills-gap study on nine sectors/subsectors completed and report disseminated in 2017
External firm has been recruited in Feb 2020 to conduct fiduciary reviews. FY 2018-19 and FY19-20 external Audit has completed.
